paper.title: Algorithm 769: FORTRAN subroutines for approximate solution of sparse quadratic assignment problems using GRASP
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 23(2), 196 (1997); collected as ACM TOMS Algorithm 769
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/769.gz (ACM article not read; no ACM fetch attempted this wake)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 769.gz (fetched by scout 2026-11-27 09:34Z into a fresh /tmp directory, unpacked as text with a splitter and not executed)
code.note: Shell archive with driver.f (driver for subroutine gqaps), src.f (GRASP subroutines gqaps and their helpers), data (the 6-by-6 test matrices), res (the shipped reference output of driver.f with data) and a Makefile. The driver reads data and the seed is fixed at 270001 inside driver.f.

field: numerics (combinatorial optimisation: quadratic assignment by GRASP)

claim.seed: 270001 (set in driver.f as seed = 270001 and passed to gqaps; the GRASP random generator uses this state)
claim.location: Shipped reference output res, block 'output', line 'cost of best permutation found'. Claim value: 4490, reached after 1000 GRASP iterations with look4 = -1, alpha = 0.25, beta = 0.50, on the data file of the archive.
claim.metric: Cost of the best permutation found by GRASP for the 6-by-6 quadratic assignment test instance, as printed by outsol (integer).
claim.paper_value: The paper's own experiments are not read. The value is the shipped res output for the archive's own test data.

tolerance.basis: The cost is an integer and is printed exactly, so a different cost differs by at least 1. The tolerance 0.5 accepts only the exact integer; it is fixed now, before any run, and not to be loosened after a run. The best permutation printed in res is also expected to match, but the claim is the cost.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: 1000 GRASP iterations on a 6-by-6 instance.
cost.data_size: Under 1 KB: the data file in the archive.
cost.data_licence: No data beyond the archive. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The shipped driver runs a seeded randomized GRASP heuristic and prints the cost of its best permutation, so a rerun must run the Fortran code with the same seed to reproduce the integer cost; the value is not a closed form.
